lessonRef.title: Guided practice: hydration across the day

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 4: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice hydration across the day. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Different people get thirsty at different points in the day depending on their own schedule and activities.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app
learner-local: a cup or container to notice water intake with
learner-local: a way to check the time

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one advantage of choosing your own hydration check-in times based on your real schedule instead of following a fixed schedule someone else set.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Schedule ownership: All three check-in times are specific and tied to the learner's own real schedule. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately judges whether their chosen times caught real thirst signals and names any point their schedule missed. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner run the same self-chosen-schedule approach on a day with a different routine, such as a day with an activity or outing versus a quiet day at home, and compare whether their best check-in times changed between the two kinds of days.

resources.title: hydration across the day coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Different people get thirsty at different points in the day depending on their own schedule and activities.
Coach direction: Before picking your check-in times, think about your actual day today, not an ideal day.
Learner prompt: List three points in your real schedule today, like right after you wake up, mid-morning, or after an activity, when you could realistically pause to notice thirst.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: hydration across the day complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Choose your own three check-in times from your list and stick to them today. At each one, notice how thirsty you actually feel and roughly how much water you've had since your last check-in, then write both down.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I picked three specific times from my own real schedule, not times someone else chose for me.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I noticed and recorded a thirst level at all three of my chosen times.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I noticed and recorded roughly how much water I had between check-ins.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: hydration across the day minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one advantage of choosing your own hydration check-in times based on your real schedule instead of following a fixed schedule someone else set.

Success checks: Schedule ownership: All three check-in times are specific and tied to the learner's own real schedule. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately judges whether their chosen times caught real thirst signals and names any point their schedule missed.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: hydration across the day supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional hydration across the day condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Schedule ownership: All three check-in times are specific and tied to the learner's own real schedule. | Self-evaluation of the plan: The learner accurately judges whether their chosen times caught real thirst signals and names any point their schedule missed..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
